key_insight: The paper shows that humanoid robots can be designed and controlled with human safety as a first-class objective, not an afterthought. By jointly optimizing hardware and motion for both locomotion and human-related metrics, ergoCub walks more robustly while reducing spinal load.
problem_solved: Humanoid robots often optimize for performance alone, which can create motions or designs that are unsafe or physically demanding for nearby humans. This work addresses the challenge of building robots that are both effective and human-aware at the hardware and control levels.
method: Use a shared embodied intelligence framework to jointly optimize robot design and motion control.
Include human-centric metrics, such as back stress/spinal load, alongside standard locomotion objectives.
Develop and test the ergoCub humanoid robot to evaluate safety-aware walking performance and robustness.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this highlights a practical path toward deploying embodied AI systems that balance performance with human safety. It suggests that optimization objectives should include human impact metrics, especially for robots operating in shared spaces.

paper_title: Towards shared embodied intelligence in humanoid robots through optimization, development and testing of the human-aware ergoCub robot
paper_authors: Carlotta Sartore, Mohamed Elobaid, Lorenzo Rapetti, Giulio Romualdi, Stefano Dafarra
